---
title: "Development"
---

```bash
composer install
composer test        # polyfill only
composer test:ext    # with the extension loaded from .ext/libphit.dylib
```

The composer scripts run the tests with the PHP that runs Composer, so
`php85 "$(which composer)" test` picks a version. Any PHP 8.3 or later works.
`composer test:ext` needs the PHP that `.ext/libphit.dylib` was built for;
under another one the extension does not load and the parity tests skip.

## Tests

- `tests/Unit` holds ports of the extension's own test suites. They call the
  polyfill directly through `Polyfill::implementation()`, so they test it
  whether or not the extension is loaded.
- `tests/Parity` runs only with the extension loaded. It compares the polyfill
  with the extension on the reference fixtures, on stress and adversarial
  inputs, and on seeded random inputs.

## Reference fixtures

`tests/fixtures/REFERENCE` pins the phit commit that the polyfill reproduces.
`bin/fetch-fixtures [checkout]` copies that commit's R, SciPy, mpmath, and API
fixtures into `tests/fixtures`. The copies are committed and never edited by
hand.

`bin/generate-bootstrap` regenerates `bootstrap.php` and `src/FunctionMap.php`
from phit's API contract (`tests/fixtures/php-api.json`). A function is
declared only when its implementation exists.

## Site data

The benchmark and verification files on this site are generated by scripts
in the repository:

```bash
# Benchmarks: polyfill and extension in one process, OPcache without the JIT.
php -d extension=libphit.so -d opcache.enable_cli=1 -d opcache.jit=disable \
    benchmarks/site.php

# Parity log, then the PHP version and JIT matrix, then the verification files.
PARITY_LOG=build/parity.json php -d extension=libphit.so vendor/bin/pest tests/Parity
php bin/site-matrix --out=build/matrix.jsonl --extension=libphit.so
php bin/site-data --parity=build/parity.json --matrix=build/matrix.jsonl
```

`bin/accuracy-report` prints the reference tables in `ACCURACY.md`.
